{"status":"candidate","chosen_option":"prefix_sums","assumptions":["Input is well-formed as described.","Python integers can represent all possible range sums."],"observations":[{"statement":"The program must use Python 3.11 and only the standard library, reading stdin and writing stdout.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"There are n signed integers and q inclusive, one-based ranges; output one sum per range.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"The examples exercise a single-element negative range and multiple ranges over negative and positive values.","source_ids":["public1","public2"]}],"artifact":{"code":"import sys


def main():
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()))
    n, q = data[0], data[1]
    values = data[2:2 + n]

    prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, value in enumerate(values, 1):
        prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] + value

    offset = 2 + n
    output = []
    for i in range(q):
        left, right = data[offset + 2 * i], data[offset + 2 * i + 1]
        output.append(str(prefix[right] - prefix[left - 1]))

    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(output))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
